scene_report.narration_text: In March 2024, Kendrick Lamar ignited a massive controversy by rejecting the 'Big Three' rap classification.
scene_report.main_action: gesturing dismissively with his hand while speaking into a studio microphone

scene_report.narration_text: Kendrick Lamar asserted there was only one king, prompting Drake to fire back with the track Push Ups.
scene_report.main_action: typing on a laptop keyboard to release a track

scene_report.narration_text: Kendrick Lamar then unleashed the six-minute diss track Euphoria to attack his rival.
scene_report.visual_focus: Kendrick Lamar's hand on the mixing fader
scene_report.main_action: adjusting audio mixing faders on a soundboard

scene_report.narration_text: The conflict turned personal when Drake released Family Matters, making explosive allegations about Kendrick's private life.
scene_report.main_action: holding a smartphone displaying a social media post

scene_report.narration_text: Less than an hour later, Kendrick Lamar shocked listeners with Meet the Grahams, firing back with disturbing claims.
scene_report.main_action: staring intensely at a computer monitor showing a waveform

scene_report.narration_text: On May 4, Kendrick Lamar dropped the devastating track Not Like Us, accusing Drake of serious misconduct.
scene_report.main_action: pressing a 'publish' button on a digital interface

scene_report.narration_text: Although Drake denied these allegations, the song exploded across the internet as a global anthem.
scene_report.main_action: shaking his head while looking at a tablet

scene_report.narration_text: This battle for the rap throne ultimately became one of hip-hop's most unforgettable rivalries.
scene_report.main_action: standing on a stage with a microphone

scene_report.narration_text: According to the supplied account, the song Not Like Us achieved significant recognition, winning five Grammy Awards.
scene_report.main_action: resting on a velvet display stand
